prompt:
A hand-painted map of a whole continent seen from directly above, in the manner of a painted fantasy map such as a map of Middle-earth: coastlines, mountain ranges drawn as shaded ridges, rivers as fine dark lines running downhill to the sea, forests as textured masses, marsh, desert and open plain each in its own tone. Oil on parchment in a 19th-century academic manner with a smooth, finely blended surface, soft glazed transitions, fine detail, no heavy impasto. Palette of umber, ochre, gold, olive and sea-green with near-black shading. Less detail at larger scale; nothing drawn smaller than a hill or a wood; no settlements, no roads, no figures, no borders between countries. No text, no lettering, no compass rose, no scale bar, no frame, no grid, not photographic. The whole sheet is land and sea; nothing is cut off at the edges.

One large landmass fills a square sheet, north at the top. Sea-green sea runs down the whole west edge and along the whole south edge, each a strip about a tenth of the sheet wide, meeting at the south-west corner; the land runs unbroken to the north and east edges. A high broken mountain range runs west to east across the northern fifth of the land, widest and highest in its middle with snow on its peaks and many notched passes; at its western end it breaks down into wooded hills, and at its eastern end the mountains open into a ring around one wide, flat, high basin of pale green, with a river crossing the basin floor and leaving it southward through a narrow gap. In the north-west, below the western end of the range, lies dark dense forest over crumpled, folded hills with many small steep valleys. Down the west, a single great dark old forest of lowland covers the land nearly to the west coast; a river comes out of the middle of the continent and runs west along the southern edge of this forest to the western sea, with a wide belt of dark green marsh and reed between the forest and the river. In the south-west, a second old forest, lighter and more broken, stands on pale limestone ground: pale ribs of rock show through the trees and the ground is pocked with many small round dark sinkholes; toward the south-west coast this forest thins into marsh. In the south, a wide slow river runs from the middle of the continent south through open olive-green meadow and farmed lowland to the southern sea, ending in a sheltered bay. In the south-east, streams gather in low hills and become one broad river running south-east through pale green flood meadows to join another river before reaching the southern sea. The whole east is wide pale gold grass steppe; the river from the high basin runs south through it, and in the middle of the steppe it divides into many threads through a long patch of dark reed marsh before running on south to the sea; beside it a band of paler hard ground runs north to south. In the exact middle of the continent lies open brown upland heath, a wide shallow bowl ringed by worn low hills, and in the middle of that bowl one long dark hill with the plain outline of a great animal lying curled asleep.
